A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R-MCTS and search-based learning work, despite v4's EXACT branding. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VisualWebArena experiments, fine-tuning results, compute-scaling experiments, ablations, and error analyses, including additional browser and task-instruction experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds R-MCTS evaluations on WebArena's GitLab domain and OSWorld, alongside additional comparison results.

M1.justification: v4 adds an OSWorld-specific search adaptation: breadth starts at 10 and decays exponentially with depth, whereas v1 documents fixed breadth. The core reflection, debate, and training procedures remain unchanged. Best-in-Tree SFT and Tree-Traversal SFT are renamed Imitation Learning and Exploratory Learning.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only VisualWebArena. v4 retains its three environments and adds WebArena's GitLab tasks in Table 2 and OSWorld's desktop, file-operation, and multi-application tasks in Tables 3-4. This substantially broadens the environments and task requirements evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the flat ReAct reference with Best-of-N ReAct. New OSWorld comparisons include Agent-S, AgentStore variants, and Learn-by-Interact, using reported external results where indicated. Appendix Table 8 adds broader VWA comparisons, including ICAL and additional model-based agents. Existing VWA comparators remain.

E3.justification: v4 introduces separate OSWorld protocols using screenshot plus accessibility-tree inputs and accessibility-tree-only inputs, a 15-step limit, a 60-node search limit, and depth-decaying breadth starting at 10. These are settings for added experiments; the existing VWA settings and learning-data counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revised compute-scaling analysis in Figure 1 compares R-MCTS with increasing Best-of-N ReAct computation, providing an additional check against repeated sampling. Component ablations, difficulty breakdowns, the qualitative example, error analysis, and Appendix B browser and task-instruction studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables and curve in v4 continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results: GitLab success reaches 23.5% for R-MCTS with MAD; OSWorld R-MCTS achieves 19.39% with screenshot plus accessibility-tree inputs and 16.6% with accessibility-tree-only inputs. Figure 1 adds Best-of-N results, and Table 8 adds leaderboard entries. Matched VWA, fine-tuning, and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, policy/value definitions, reflection-error equations, and Appendix A search equations and pseudocode are retained. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations appear.

C1.justification: v4 foregrounds Exploratory Learning within EXACT and frames the approach as building o1-like agents, while treating Imitation Learning as conventional. The headline changes from 97% performance recovery with roughly fourfold savings to Exploratory Learning's 87% recovery and 2.7-fold savings. These summarize different retained rows, rather than changed performance for one method.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new OSWorld results as evidence of broader applicability and competitive performance using a single model, while distinguishing comparators that use additional resources, specialized models, or training. Existing mechanism explanations, error interpretations, and Section 8 limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new OSWorld search configuration and newly states that EXACT's system prompts slightly modify ReAct prompts to encourage exploration. It also clarifies that vision fine-tuning was unavailable at study time and updates the supplied code/data link. Appendix implementation and prompt details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references and comparison-oriented discussion for OSWorld, Agent-S, AgentStore, and Learn-by-Interact, emphasizing differences in resource use. It also positions best-action training as traditional imitation learning. Section 6's broader literature discussion and principal priority claim remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and learning-related paragraphs are revised around EXACT and Exploratory Learning, with terminology updated throughout. The section sequence and most background, method, analysis, limitations, and appendix prose remain intact; this is focused rewriting rather than wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the comparative displays through two OSWorld tables, the appendix leaderboard, and GitLab columns in Table 2. Figure 1 gains a Best-of-N curve, learning diagrams are relabeled, and the learning-results table gains a Search column. Existing appendix displays are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens empirical validation of R-MCTS beyond v1's VWA-only evidence. GitLab and OSWorld test materially different environments, while Figure 1's Best-of-N comparison makes the compute-scaling evidence more informative than the earlier flat ReAct reference. The learning evidence remains unchanged, and limited Best-of-N procedural detail and differing comparator resources constrain interpretation, but the broader validation provides a substantial net quality gain.
